strings.name: Vas Narasimhan
strings.summary: With an educational background in medicine and public policy, Vas Narasimhan joined Novartis in 2005 and became CEO in 2018. He has led its focus on innovative medicines, with the Alcon and Sandoz spin-offs completed during his tenure. In 2026 he joined Anthropic's board.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Only the officially confirmed birth year, 1976, is retained. MD and research PhD, spin-offs and sales, board service and scientific contributions, and clinical or business forecasts and achieved results are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads Novartis, advancing innovative drug development and the business focus of a multinational pharmaceutical company.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Bachelor's in biological sciences from the University of Chicago in 1998; MD and master's in public policy from Harvard in 2003.
strings.facts.f2.label: Early career
strings.facts.f2.value: Worked at McKinsey before joining Novartis, subsequently holding roles in vaccines, drug development and group management.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Focus on innovative medicines
strings.highlights.h1.text: The spin-offs of Alcon's eye care devices and Sandoz's generics and biosimilars businesses were completed during his tenure.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Board service across sectors
strings.highlights.h2.text: Appointed to Anthropic's board by its Long-Term Benefit Trust in 2026; this does not make him a Trust member or the sole creator of AI medical advances.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Participates in third-quarter earnings call
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed business, R&D and capital allocation and answered analysts' questions on the earnings call.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Joins Anthropic's board
strings.timeline.t2.text: The Long-Term Benefit Trust announced his appointment as a director of Anthropic.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Sandoz spin-off completed
strings.timeline.t3.text: Novartis spun off its generics and biosimilars business into an independent company.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Alcon spin-off completed
strings.timeline.t4.text: The eye care devices business became independent; Novartis retained its ophthalmology medicines business.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes Novartis CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Joseph Jimenez; the appointment was announced on September 4, 2017.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Leads global drug development
strings.timeline.t6.text: Served as Novartis's global head of drug development and chief medical officer until 2018.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Novartis
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began holding roles related to commercial operations, development and strategy at the company.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes medicine and public policy studies at Harvard
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned an MD and a master's in public policy, not a research PhD.
